newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT-Coffee risks move lower, due unchanged.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-Coffee risks move lower, due unchanged.

text.p: Close * Support * Resist * RSI14 * MA10 * MA40
LIFFE coffee risks pushing back down, technical analysts said on Friday.
Traders called benchmark September to open unchanged.
The market might dip down to $1,530 a tonne, but was probably in the process of building a new, lower range, Adrian Haylor, technical analyst at Sucden, said.
"Thursday's high of $1,645 might be the full extent of the upswing," he said.
Strong resistance was at $1,700 and then up to $1,750, making a push upwards hard work.
"I wouldn't be surprised to see the market heading down," he said.
But he did not expect a collapse. "It's not going to fall out of bed."
New York coffee futures ended weaker in uneventful dealings on Thursday in what traders said was mainly a local-dominated market.
Robusta coffee-growing regions were likely to be affected by the cyclical El Nino weather pattern developing in the Pacific, UK trade house E D & F Man said on Thursday.

El Nino, which scientists say will not peak until December 1997 and could be almost as severe as that of 1992/83 -- this century's worst -- was overwhelmingly a phenomenon of the robusta market, the firm said in its June/July coffee report.
No damaging cold was in sight for the next five days in Brazil's coffee regions, independent forecaster Weather Services Corporation said.
